learning_outcomes.text: Explain the perceptual and cognitive foundations of visual encoding, including pre-attentive processing, memory, attention and the effectiveness ranking of visual channels.

Decompose a complex problem into data and task abstractions and select and defend appropriate encodings and layouts for tabular, temporal, network, tree-structured, scalar-field, vector-field and spatial data.

Implement interactive, data-driven visualizations for the web using a declarative or data-binding visualization library, including selection, filtering, navigation, brushing and linking, and coordinated multiple views that support an identified analysis task.
Apply aggregation, clustering and dimensionality-reduction techniques to make large datasets tractable for visual analysis and describe the distortions each technique introduces.

Critique and evaluate visualization designs against established design principles and through appropriate evaluation methods and communicate the findings and resulting insights to a technical audience in writing and in an oral presentation.
